answer: An agent marketplace weights governance votes by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count, and snapshots eligible stake at dawn before each ballot. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight: a tide of accounts cannot turn a whisper into a majority. An attacker must acquire and immobilize enough real capital to outweigh honest voters, sacrificing liquidity for the full lock period.
